change: seventeen cyber quiz pages move onto the server render path, and the lesson they file under stops coming from the handle
_context: Units 2 to 5 each shipped their own answer key in the page body, so a teacher
locking a quiz locked a column and not the questions. Migrating the bank to
quiz_bank is what makes the lock enforceable; the Matrixify sheet that strips
the key from the page is a human import and is NOT part of this deploy.
The defect worth reading is not the migration. The extractor read the lesson
out of the Shopify handle, which is right for Units 2, 4 and 5 and wrong for
every page in Unit 3: that unit was renumbered onto the Fall 2026 CED in the
page BODIES and not in the handles, so ap-cyber-unit-3-lesson-5-quiz is topic
3.4. Six banks were one lesson too high, 3.1a and 3.1b collapsed into one, and
nothing threw anywhere. It was caught by making two resolvers agree.
A second defect came out of the same pass: smoke/quiz-bank-authoring.js and
the extractor each kept their own copy of the no-CED-citation rule, and the
extractor's was narrower. Four unit-4 stems saying 'according to the AP CED'
extracted clean. One module now, both callers.

checks.name: the bank lands on the lesson the gradebook keys, agreed by two resolvers
no CED citation reaches a student, in ANY bank this repo seeds
THE ONE THAT SHIPPED: read the lesson out of the handle
checks._why: This is the state the extractor was in. Unit 3 files one lesson high and 3.1 collapses to a single column. It must go red.

checks.name: CED topic 3.1 collapses into one gradebook column
checks._why: 3.1 is taught over two pages and keys 3.1a and 3.1b. Pairing handle to lesson by position is what keeps them apart; take the first every time and a better score on one part masks the other.

checks.name: a page that contradicts the taxonomy is guessed at rather than refused
checks._why: One source is how the mis-filing happened. A disagreement means one of them moved, and either answer is a guess.
checks.expect_failure: a page whose h1 contradicts the taxonomy is refused

checks.name: a CED citation in a bank OUTSIDE the scoped course and unit
checks._why: Section 1 of that suite drives ap-cybersecurity unit-1 only, so the seventeen banks added here were checked by nothing. Injecting a citation into every prompt in the new seed must be seen by the global sweep, and must NOT be seen by section 1, which is how the sweep is shown to be more than a second copy.
checks.expect_failure: locations, 0 citations in prompts or options

checks.name: unit 3 serves the RENUMBERED lessons, which did not exist before this deploy
checks._why: 3.1b, 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4 all answered 404 in production before this change, and the handle-digit reading would have produced 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5 instead. This assertion is false yesterday in both directions.
checks.command: for L in 3.1a 3.1b 3.2 3.3 3.4; do curl -sS --max-time 20 "https://progress.apcsexamprep.com/api/quiz/ap-cybersecurity/unit-3/$L/quiz" -o /dev/null -w "$L=%{http_code} "; done; echo

checks.name: and 3.5 does NOT, because its page carries ten questions and was held back
checks._why: A teacher bundle instrument is 9 to 24 items and every web quiz measured is 5 or 6. Over the ceiling is a refusal, so this stays 404 until a human says what that page is. A gate that only checked the successes would not notice the refusal had quietly stopped working.

checks.name: seventeen banks are live, sized 5, and anonymous gets no question from any of them
checks._why:
Asserted 'anonymous receives 5 questions' first, and that FAILED against a correct production: every one of the seventeen is locked for anonymous callers, which is the point of the anonymous gate shipped in #585. An anonymous caller who got five questions would be the defect. The loopback rehearsal passed only because a throwaway database has no classes and so no gate rows.
routes/quiz.js:249 looks the bank up BEFORE the gate and 404s an empty one, and the locked response still reports pool = rows.length. So pool is the anonymously visible proof the bank landed, and it is false before this deploy in both directions: these locations 404'd entirely, and the wrong reading of the handle would have put unit 3's pools on 3.2 to 3.5 instead of 3.1a to 3.4.
checks.command: node -e "const T=[['unit-2','2.1'],['unit-2','2.2'],['unit-2','2.4'],['unit-3','3.1a'],['unit-3','3.1b'],['unit-3','3.2'],['unit-3','3.3'],['unit-3','3.4'],['unit-4','4.2'],['unit-4','4.3'],['unit-4','4.4'],['unit-5','5.1'],['unit-5','5.2'],['unit-5','5.3'],['unit-5','5.4'],['unit-5','5.5'],['unit-5','5.6']];(async()=>{let pool5=0,leaked=0,missing=0;for(const [u,l] of T){const r=await fetch('https://progress.apcsexamprep.com/api/quiz/ap-cybersecurity/'+u+'/'+encodeURIComponent(l)+'/quiz');if(r.status===404){missing++;continue;}const j=await r.json().catch(()=>null);if(j&&j.pool===5)pool5++;const qs=(j&&j.questions)||[];if(qs.length||qs.some(q=>q.correct_index!==undefined||q.explanation!==undefined))leaked++;}console.log('pool5='+pool5+'/17 missing='+missing+' leaked='+leaked);})()"
